name: Cardiac macrophage
short_description: Resident scavenger cell of the heart with a rare second job: an elongated, spindled macrophage wedged between cardiomyocytes that not only clears debris but couples to the muscle cells through connexin-43 gap junctions and helps carry the electrical impulse through the atrioventricular node.

textbook.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; used as final on first attempt. Exactly the house textbook look: a muted, desaturated educational palette of soft dusty tints with thin clean outlines and gentle soft shading on a neutral dark-charcoal ground - no bright cartoon fills, no heavy black strokes, and not a monochrome line drawing. Science reads correctly: a single elongated spindled pale-sage macrophage with two tapering ends and fine filopodia, wedged into the diagonal interstitial cleft between two dusty-rose cardiomyocytes whose cross-striation is clearly drawn; one small eccentric kidney-shaped blue-violet nucleus with a nucleolus; a Golgi stack beside it; three brown mitochondria; numerous small magenta lysosomes; one pale phagosome holding grey engulfed debris fragments (self debris, not bacteria); and - the point of the figure - a row of teal connexin-43 hemichannel barrels bridging the macrophage membrane to the upper myocyte's lateral sarcolemma, drawn as discrete plaques rather than a full intercalated disc. None of the do-NOT-draw items appear: not a round free-floating monocyte, one nucleus only, no cell wall or nucleoid, no cilia or flagella, no infection scene. Diagonal composition leaves clean dark margins upper-left and lower-right for leader lines. No baked text, no border, background fills all four edges)

sem.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; used as final on first attempt. Correct false-colour surface-only SEM: a pale blue-green spindled macrophage lying lengthwise along - and partly moulded around - a warm bronze cardiomyocyte whose sarcomere cross-banding is legible as fine transverse ridges, with a second fibre and a dark out-of-focus interstitial cleft behind. The surface detail is exactly what the reference calls for: broad lamellipodial veils at the cell margins, dense membrane ruffles over the body, and long fine filopodia gripping the myocyte surface on both sides. Correctly shows no internal organelles and no cutaway (an SEM cannot see them), shallow depth of field, cool studio microscopy lighting. No baked text, no scale bar, no border)

3d.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; used as final on first attempt. Natural believable biological tints, neither near-monochrome nor neon: a translucent pale sage-green plasma membrane with visible subsurface scattering over a warm amber cytoplasm, a large pale blue-violet reniform nucleus with nucleolus and a clear indentation, two ochre mitochondria with drawn cristae, a grey-green Golgi stack, scattered crimson lysosomes, and a pale phagosome containing grey debris chunks. The macrophage is spindled with lamellipodial veils and long filopodia and lies diagonally in the cleft between two dusty-rose striated cardiomyocytes. The connexin-43 plaque is rendered as a cluster of individual cyan connexon barrels docked across the macrophage-myocyte contact with a soft glow, which makes the coupling the visual focus. One nucleus, no bacteria, no wall or nucleoid. Clean seamless dark studio background reaching all four edges, no text, no border)

watercolor.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; used as final on first attempt. Warm aged paper with foxing speckles fills the entire frame corner to corner - sampled pixel values at all four edges are cream, with no mat, frame, drop shadow, vignette or sheet-lying-on-a-surface - and a soft grey-indigo wash halo sits directly on the paper behind the subject. Fine ink linework over translucent washes in the naturalist-atlas manner: pale sage spindled macrophage with ruffled margins and filopodia lying in the cleft between two rose cardiomyocytes painted with delicate cross-striation, one blue-violet kidney-shaped nucleus, teal Golgi, ochre mitochondria, crimson lysosomes, a phagosome with grey debris, and a diagonal row of teal connexin-43 barrels at the upper myocyte contact. No text, no border. Sole blemish: a faint pale crescent stroke in the cytoplasm just left of the phagosome that at 4x zoom can read as a stray letter C; at page size it is invisible and it does not touch any labelled structure, so it did not warrant burning a re-render)

reference: pass as a generic tissue-resident-macrophage ultrastructure plate, NOT a cardiac one (Wikimedia Commons "Macrophage in the alveolus Lung - TEM.jpg", public domain, Louisa Howard / Dartmouth Electron Microscope Facility). No freely-licensed micrograph of a cardiac resident macrophage - let alone one showing connexin-43 coupling at the AV node - exists in Commons or another clearly reusable source; the published images of that cell, including those in Hulsmans et al. 2017, are not relicensable here, and section 2 of the render log states this plainly. What the plate does show truthfully, at a magnification where it matters, is a tissue-resident macrophage in situ: one huge deeply indented lobed reniform nucleus cut in section (both the large right lobe and the smaller lower-left lobe are the same nucleus) with coarsely clumped peripheral heterochromatin, granular cytoplasm, numerous mitochondria with visible cristae, and small dense lysosomal granules. It does NOT show the elongated spindled shape, the cardiomyocyte contact or the connexin-43 plaques - those come from the literature and are carried by the four illustrated styles. Cleaned with edit_image.py: the baked-in instrument caption ("01LungTEM ...") and the white letterbox bars top and bottom were removed and a natural false-colour applied (blue-violet nucleus, warm bronze-amber cytoplasm, reddish-brown mitochondria and dense granules) while keeping the electron-micrograph grain. Attempts 2 and 3 mis-coloured the lower nuclear lobe sepia as if it were a second structure; attempt 4 (gemini-3-pro-image) colours the whole indented nucleus consistently and is the cleaned display image
decision: use as final on first attempt; muted educational palette with thin outlines, every reference structure present, connexin-43 plaques at the myocyte contact make the coupling explicit. Chosen as the SVG label base
